transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you, and thank you so much for taking the time to see me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your day. 

Um... I guess I'm here because... well, it's a little embarrassing to talk about, to be honest, and I really don't want you to think badly of me. But for nearly two years now, I've just been so sure that our contractor and, well, some of the people on my block, are quietly working together to cheat us. They're keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, and it's just been very stressful. 

My husband keeps showing me all these receipts to try and make me feel better, and the workers always have so many excuses, but... I just know what they're doing. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want to sound like a difficult person or a complainer, I just don't know what else to do. Am I explaining that okay?
Have you noticed any other changes in your health, such as difficulties with your memory, confusion, or any physical symptoms like headaches or weakness?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. My memory is still quite good, thankfully, and I haven't felt confused at all. And no headaches or weakness, either. I'm actually in very good health, physically. I really try to take good care of myself so I don't become a burden to my husband or anyone else. 

I hope that's a helpful answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that other people around you cannot hear?

Oh, my goodness, no. Um... no, nothing like that at all. I know sometimes people might wonder about that when someone is as... well, as stressed as I am, but I promise I don't hear any voices or anything strange. 

I only hear what's really there, just regular everyday noises. I just happen to notice the things the contractors are doing, that's all. I really hope you don't think I'm... you know, losing my mind or anything like that. I'm just a very observant person, I think. Did I answer that okay for you?
Are there any other people, aside from your contractor and neighbors, who you feel are involved in this situation or acting against you?

Oh, um... no, I don't believe so. It's really just the contractor and... well, those few neighbors who seem to be coordinating with him. I haven't noticed anyone else acting strangely or trying to cause trouble for us. 

I really try to get along with everyone, you know? I'm not the sort of person who goes around looking for conflicts or thinking everyone is out to get me. It's just this one specific situation with the kitchen that's been so... so difficult to ignore. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right picture of what's going on.
Even when your husband shows you those receipts and the workers provide their explanations, are you able to consider the possibility that you might be mistaken about their intentions?

Oh... well, I know my husband tries so hard to make me feel better with those receipts, and the workers always have such, um, reasonable-sounding excuses. And I really, really want to believe them, I do. I don't want to be a difficult person or cause a fuss. 

But... oh dear, it's just so hard because... well, I've been so sure for nearly two years now. It just feels like the contractor and some of the people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us. Like they're keeping my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, no matter what those papers say. 

I know that probably sounds terrible, and I'm so sorry if it seems like I'm just being stubborn. I really try to be open-minded, but it's just this strong feeling I can't shake. Am I explaining that alright? I hope I'm not coming across as too unreasonable... I just want to be honest with you.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to organize your thoughts, or have you felt like your ideas are being interfered with or taken from your mind?

Oh, goodness, no. No, my thoughts are perfectly fine. I mean... I still manage all the household bills and keep everything organized just like I always have. 

I don't feel like anyone is interfering with my mind or... or taking my ideas, if that's what you mean. That sounds very frightening, but thankfully, I haven't experienced anything like that. My mind is just my own. I just get a bit overwhelmed with the kitchen situation, but my thoughts are clear. 

Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. I promise I'm keeping track of everything just fine up here.
Aside from the stress you've described, has this situation with your kitchen affected your ability to socialize with friends or attend to your usual daily responsibilities?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I really try not to let it ruin everything else, you know? I want to be a good neighbor and a good friend. 

Outside of dealing with the whole remodel... mess, I still keep up with everything. I go to my church gatherings every week, and I wouldn't miss my book club for the world. I still do all my usual household routines, cooking and cleaning, and I'm always making plans with the family. 

I really do function quite normally, I promise. I don't just sit around obsessing over the kitchen all day. I hope that shows that I'm still handling things well? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm falling apart or anything like that.
If you were to see definitive, indisputable evidence that the contractor was not cheating you, would you be able to accept that you were mistaken?

Oh... well... I want to say yes. I really, really do. I know that's what I should say, and I'd love nothing more than to just... put this all behind me and tell my husband he was right all along. 

But... oh, doctor, if I'm being perfectly honest with you—and I do want to be a good patient and give you the truth—it's just... well, it's been nearly two years. Two whole years of feeling this way. And even with all the receipts my husband brings me, and all the excuses the workers give... I just can't shake this certainty I have. It just feels so clear to me that the contractor, and maybe a few of the neighbors, are quietly working together to cheat us. To just... keep the kitchen half-wrong on purpose. 

I know that sounds so stubborn, and I'm so sorry. I really don't want to be a difficult person. But even if you showed me something that looked like perfect proof... I think a part of me would still believe they're just very, very good at hiding what they're doing. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think too badly of me for saying that... I'm just trying to be as honest as I can be.
